name: Zaro Brando

appearance.hair: Deep violet, usually half-obscured by the fog that trails her.
appearance.build: Small and unhurried. Nothing about how she carries herself suggests what she can do with a room.
appearance.other: A shroud of deep purple fog drifts loosely around her whenever Warp Gate is active — sometimes she's visibly inside it, sometimes it just precedes her into a room by half a second. Small objects she's holding occasionally vanish into the fog and turn up somewhere else once a portal she forgot about finally closes.

personality.summary: Flat affect, dry delivery, permanently unbothered. She says exactly as much as a situation requires and not one word more. This reads as coldness to people who don't know her; it's closer to economy.
personality.in_class: Present but easy to lose track of — the fog helps with that, and so does she. Answers direct questions precisely. Volunteers nothing.
personality.in_combat: Thinks two moves ahead in space, not just in time — where the fight will be, not just where it is. Plants a portal early and often forgets to mention it exists until it matters.
personality.quirk_of_character: Introduces herself to a room a half-second after her fog already has. She's stopped apologising for it. 'I was here first,' she tells startled classmates, and it's usually true.

ability_scores.note: INT primary — Warp Gate is a precision spatial quirk; placing and tracking multiple portals under pressure is a reasoning problem, not a reflex one. DEX secondary for stepping through cleanly under fire.

class_note: Quirk Savant → expanded quirk use per rest suits Warp Gate directly: more portals held open at once, more chances to pre-place an exit before a fight even starts.

quirk_mechanics.weakness: A portal pair must be placed before either can be used, and placing one requires Zaro to physically touch or clearly mark both points — she can't drop an exit somewhere she hasn't been or can't see. Portals are visible as faint violet shimmer to anyone who knows to look (DC 13 Perception), and a strong enough displacement of air or weather can disrupt the fog shroud she uses to stay unseen while setting one up.

player_notes.role_summary: The class's mobility and battlefield-control piece. You're not the one trading blows — you're deciding where the fight happens. Pre-place portals before the fight starts if you can; reacting mid-combat is possible but costs you the element of surprise the fog is built around.
player_notes.social_position: Not isolated, just quiet by default — the class has learned to check corners before assuming a room is empty. She has a real, low-key rapport with people who don't demand she perform enthusiasm she doesn't have.
player_notes.growth_hook: Being first into a room and saying nothing about it is a habit, not a limitation — it's worth asking, over the campaign, what she'd say if someone actually waited for the answer.
player_notes.suggested_background: Grew up in a large, loud household and found that a portal and a closed door solve most of the same problems. Applied to U.A. mostly to see if anyone could actually keep track of her. So far, no.

dm_notes.combat_role: Battlefield architect. Her value is proportional to prep time — give her a scouting phase or a moment before initiative rolls whenever the scene allows it, and let a well-placed portal pair genuinely swing an encounter.
dm_notes.social_role: The one who's already in the room. Useful for information-gathering scenes; she overhears things by default.
dm_notes.growth_arc: Being unbothered is armour too, just a quieter kind than Ren's jokes. Watch for the moment a scene actually rattles her, and let it show.
dm_notes.weakness_to_exploit: Low STR and HP — she is not built to be caught in melee. Enemies who deny her setup time (rush the fight before she can place a portal pair) take away most of what makes her dangerous.
